newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: OAU team to visit Zaire in search for peace.
newsitem.headline: OAU team to visit Zaire in search for peace.

text.p: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) said on Wednesday it was sending a team to Zaire to press for a peaceful end to crises in the Great Lakes region of central Africa.
The OAU's conflict prevention body ordered OAU Secretary-General Salim Ahmed Salim to send the team to Zaire and other regional states to express concern at the situation.
Zaire's prime minister on Monday said he had formally ordered the armed forces to recapture a swath of territory in the east seized by rebel forces in an offensive that began in October.
The OAU has backed the territorial integrity of Zaire.

The organisation also condemned the massacre in Burundi of 126 Hutu refugees by the Tutsi-dominated army on January 11 and said in view of increasing human rights violations by the army it would not consider reviewing sanctions against the country.
The 126 Hutu refugees were forced back into Burundi from Tanzania.
Regional states imposed sanctions on Burundi in July after an army coup but they have so far failed to force military ruler Pierre Buyoya to open peace negotiations with Hutu rebels.
The OAU appealed to the international community to provide assistance to refugees and displaced people in the region.
Diplomats in New York said on Tuesday Algerian diplomat Mohamed Sahnoun, who once headed the U.N. operation in Somalia, would be named a special representative to the Great Lakes region.
They said he would jointly represent the United Nations and the OAU.
